channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Ancient Jerusalem water system opens to visitors
item.description: Solomon's Pools takes a major step toward opening to the public, offering visitors a rare look at the ancient system that supplied Jerusalem during the Second Temple period.

item.title: 44 years later: Yehuda Katz, who fell in 1982, is laid to rest
item.description: Family, friends and fellow yeshiva students gather to accompany Yehuda Yekutiel Katz to his final resting place, 44 years after he went missing in the Battle of Sultan Yacoub.

item.title: Ben Gurion chaos continue
item.description: Passengers face major delays, hours-long baggage waits, as fallout from the airport strike continues into Friday morning.

item.title: New poll: Eisenkot opens six-seat lead over Likud
item.description: Yashar! surges to 26 seats as Likud falls to 20, while the center-left bloc reaches 60 seats, just one short of a Knesset majority.

item.title: Podcast: Taking a good look at ourselves
item.description: Here comes Elul: Primal urges or the spirit of prophecy?

item.title: Vance: Iran war has entered 'new phase' as US turns to economic pressure
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance says the Iran war has entered a new phase, with Washington relying on economic pressure to prevent Tehran from rebuilding.

item.title: Hochul to Mamdani: Focus on New York, not Israel
item.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul urges Mayor Zohran Mamdani to focus on city government rather than Israel amid concerns over his anti-Israel rhetoric.

item.title: Trump administration to bar Abbas from UN for second straight year
item.description: The Trump administration plans to again bar PA chairman Mahmoud Abbas from entering the US for the UN General Assembly, Israeli media reports.

item.title: Podcast: Set the captives free
item.description: Finding holiness where you least expect it.

item.title: Wise up, America!
item.description: The war of conquest against the West involves both Iran and the Muslim Brotherhood. Opinion.

item.title: Report: Netanyahu expected to appoint Interior Minister after a year
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is currently holding discussions ahead of the appointment of a new interior minister and is expected to make a decision soon, following nearly a year in which the ministry has operated without a permanent minister. Kan 11 News reported.
According to the report, the appointment will be coordinated with Shas chairman Aryeh Deri, who is expected to approve only a candidate acceptable to him. Leading candidates include Coalition Chairman Ofir Katz, Ministers Miki Zohar and Yariv Levin, and Interior Ministry Director-General Israel Ouzan.

item.title: Report: EU preparing sanctions against Israel over E1 construction
item.description: The EU is preparing sanctions against Israel if construction proceeds in E1, including possible trade, academic, security and diplomatic measures.

item.title: US imposes new sanctions on Hezbollah, cites Iran's Quds Force ties
item.description: The US imposes new sanctions on Hezbollah over its ties to Iran's Quds Force and sanctions 10 people accused of helping move cash for the Lebanese terror group.

item.title: Report: Air Force strikes four locations in southern Lebanon
item.description:
Lebanese media reported early Friday morning that the Israel Air Force carried out strikes in the town of Mansouri and in the Ali al-Taher ridge area in southern Lebanon.
Later, two additional strikes were reported in Duhayra and Kfar Rouman in southern Lebanon.

item.title: Terrorist tries to stab IDF soldier in Jenin and is eliminated
item.description:
A terrorist armed with a knife attempted to stab an IDF soldier during IDF operational activity in the Jenin area.
The soldiers responded by firing toward the terrorist and eliminating him. No IDF injuries were reported.

item.title: Podcast: The secret behind Jewish survival
item.description: Jay Shapiro examines the unique continuity of the Jewish nation, its connection to Jerusalem, and the persistence of antisemitism throughout history.

item.title: Report in Italy: Smoke grenades and fireworks found in rental apartment of two Hapoel Tel Aviv fans
item.description:
Italian media reported that 45 kilograms of smoke grenades and fireworks were found in the rented apartment of two Hapoel Tel Aviv fans who were arrested shortly before the team’s match in Bergamo.
According to the reports, Italian special forces and intelligence officers took part in the raid on the apartment.

item.title: 50,000 at Western Wall Selichot: Captivity survivors Kupershtein and Berger participate
item.description: Some 50,000 people attend second Selichot service at the Western Wall, praying for the safety of IDF soldiers and the security of Israel.

item.title: Dozens of haredim protest at Maccabim Checkpoint following arrest of draft evader
item.description:
Dozens of extremist haredim protested at the Maccabim Checkpoint near Modi’in, in protest of the arrest of a draft evader.
The evader was detained by police near the Beit Gamzu Junction and was later transferred to Military Police custody.

item.title: Woman charged with plotting ISIS-inspired attack on New York Capitol
item.description: Albany woman charged after allegedly plotting an ISIS-inspired attack on New York's Capitol and seeking explosives and a gun.

item.title: Soccer: Hapoel Tel Aviv draws with Atalanta, Maccabi Tel Aviv loses to Lugano
item.description:
Hapoel Tel Aviv on Thursday evening played to a 0-0 draw away to Italian side Atalanta in Bergamo in the first leg of the Conference League playoff round.
Meanwhile, Maccabi Tel Aviv lost 2-1 to Lugano in Switzerland and will need to win the second leg next week to overturn the deficit and advance to the league phase of the competition.

item.title: Watch | Netanyahu at pop star Eden Ben Zaken’s concert: Am Yisrael Chai
item.description: Prime Minister speaks with the singer during her concert: “It’s wonderful to be with our amazing people and with you."

item.title: Ben Gurion strike fallout | Netanyahu orders removal of Airport Workers’ chief from Likud
item.description: Netanyahu’s associates furious over the move by Pinchas Idan, chairman of the Israel Airports Authority workers’ union, prompting the Prime Minister to order his removal from Likud.

item.title: A Jewish Soul's Journey From In The Army To At Home
item.description: From war and the struggle with the enemy to marriage, education and mutual responsibility: a journey through the three circles of the Jewish soul.

item.title: 'Hamas hasn't changed': Huckabee on Israel, Trump and the Middle East
item.description: In a special Arutz Sheva interview, US Ambassador Mike Huckabee speaks out on Iran, Hamas, Syria, Israel's upcoming elections, and Trump-Netanyahu ties.

item.title: Deri warns: “They are fighting to destroy us from within"
item.description: Shas chairman launches the party’s election campaign with harsh accusations against elements within the Haredi community who, he claims, are acting on behalf of the left to harm the right-wing bloc.

item.title: Seven countries warn against Israel's E1 plan
item.description: UK, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Canada and Norway condemn the E1 tenders, warning they could damage the two-state solution and Israel's international standing.

item.title: “Enormous economic power:" Porush warns business leaders of haredi boycott
item.description: MK Meir Porush threatened to use the sector’s purchasing power, estimated at tens of billions of shekels, if what he described as the “persecution of the Haredim" continues.

item.title: Bereaved parents hit back at Eisenkot over October 7 probe
item.description: Families bereaved on October 7 accuse supporters of a state commission of inquiry of seeking a political outcome, demanding an independent panel with coalition and opposition agreement.

item.title: New York has become Habibi City
item.description: The city that saw the towers fall under the weight of planes piloted by men who invoked Allah has elected a mayor who bows to the same cultural tradition that speaks the language of those who, in other latitudes, consider the West an enemy. Opinion.
